_note: Documentation-verified. The smoke column of the record is still empty; nothing here may be treated as proven until it is filled.
_gptSizeRule: Arbitrary WIDTHxHEIGHT: both edges divisible by 16, aspect between 1:3 and 3:1, neither edge over 3840, and TOTAL PIXELS between 655,360 and 8,294,400 inclusive. Verified 2026-09-22 against the size validator in developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/image-generation (the platform.openai.com URL now redirects there). Only the two 2.5 models are offered, and both take arbitrary sizes, so there is no standard-size fallback any more.
_fluxSizeRule: Every FLUX.2 endpoint takes image_size as {width,height} and NO aspect_ratio. [dev] clamps both edges to 512-2048. [pro], [flex] and [max] (fal OpenAPI schemas, 2026-09-22) take 256-2560 per edge, both divisible by 16, max area 4,194,304 px; none documents an image input. FLUX_DIMS in the catalog satisfies all four; the 4MP tier is WITHHELD off-square via resolutionExclusions because no ratio but 1:1 reaches 4MP inside the edge limits.
_fluxProviderRate: fal quotes: dev $0.012 per megapixel (retail does NOT track it - the flat fluxTierUsd below is the deliberate 2.5x price, owner decision); pro $0.03 first MP + $0.015 per extra MP; flex $0.05 per MP; max $0.07 first MP + $0.03 per extra MP, each 'rounded up to the nearest megapixel'. fal's own 1024x1024 example prices as ONE megapixel, so 1 MP = 1,048,576 px; every FLUX_DIMS size is at or under its tier in those units. pro/flex/max retail = published rate through the margin formula.
_seedreamSizeRule: Every Seedream endpoint takes image_size as {width,height} (or presets) and no aspect_ratio. Pixel windows from the fal OpenAPI schemas 2026-09-22: v4 960x960-4096x4096; v4.5 2560x1440-4096x4096 total; v5 lite 2560x1440-3072x3072 total; v5 pro min_area 1,048,576 max_area 4,194,304. The dimension tables live in the catalog (SEEDREAM_DIMS, seedreamDims) so the offer and the request cannot drift; tiers outside a window are withheld via versionResolutions. Edit endpoints take image_urls (up to 10). Prices: v4 $0.03, v4.5 $0.04, v5 lite $0.035 flat per image; v5 pro $0.0675 for area <= 1536x1536 else $0.135 (tentative per fal), first input image free, +$0.0045 per additional input (we send one).
_nanoFastNote: Repointed 2026-09-22. It was gemini-2.5-flash-image, which Google's pricing page marks deprecated with a shutdown on 2026-10-02: every request on the fast tier would have started failing on that date. Nano Banana 2 Lite is the migration Google names. Published rate: $30/1M image output tokens, 1120 tokens for a 1K image, = $0.0336 per image.
_gptVersionNote: 2026-09-22: gpt-image-1 removed (owner decision). Later the same day gpt-image-1.5 and gpt-image-2 were removed too (owner decision, catalog 2026-09-22.4): at the same $30/1M rate version 2 medium = 2.5 high (1,756 tokens) and 2 high = 2.5 max (7,024), so it had no price point 2.5 lacks; 1.5 was $32/1M and 1K-only. OpenAI's models page lists only the two 2.5 models as image models. Flare is 'our fastest model for high-quality, everyday image generation', Sunburst 'our most capable model for image generation and editing'. Both take low, medium, high, xhigh, max and auto; we offer the five explicit ones.
_gptSizeFix: 2026-09-22: 16:9:1K and 9:16:1K were 1024x576 / 576x1024 = 589,824 px, BELOW the 655,360 minimum, so the validator rejects them outright. 1280x720 / 720x1280 (921,600 px) is the smallest 16:9 pair that clears the floor with both edges divisible by 16. This was an ordinary 16:9-at-1K request on the default version of a live family. Never observed failing against the live API - found by driving the documented validator - so one real 16:9 1K generation is still owed as proof.
_gptQualityRule: low/medium/high/xhigh/max on both 2.5 models (auto exists but is never sent: its cost depends on the generated image, so it cannot be quoted). Enforced by validateSettings against the catalog's quality list.
